proposals.evidence: DEDR 474 explicitly documents Kannada eraḍu, Kodagu daṇḍï, Kota eyḏ, Kurukh irb (two persons), Kuwi rindi, Malayalam raṇṭu, Parji adjectival ir, Tamil reṇṭu and Toda ēḍ. The survey cognacy annotations independently identify the article. Final vowels and the Kurukh personal versus Parji adjectival use are retained; no grammatical category is silently added to the generic survey gloss two. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 4682 gives Kota maṇḍ and Tulu maṇḍe head, alongside Kannada maṇḍe and the wider maṇṭai skull/head family. Survey Kota manḍə and Tulu manḍa preserve their final vowels. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR2559 directly documents Gondi hille, Kodagu ille, Kota il-, Tamil illai and Telugu lēdu in the negative existential family. Survey helle/ille/illa/lēdu preserve their attested endings and generic not gloss, without replacing them by an invented common citation form. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR497 directly gives Kannada ele/ela, Kota el, Toda es̱ and Tulu irè/ele leaf. Survey yele, ēlu, ers and ira preserve the initial glide, final-vowel and Toda sibilant transcription differences; full article and source cognacy support the same leaf family. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
